title: Host panics building and writing a single buffer over 4 GiB (repr_windows.rs u32::MAX assert) on the live host
outcome: The code path that built a single >4 GiB buffer and passed it to a Windows write is identified (component, input, size, time). It is fixed so no such buffer can be built or written, and a regression test guards it. Surviving the panic is not considered acceptable.
acceptance: A diagnosis note names the exact component and call path that produced the >4 GiB buffer at 2026-10-28T01:12:25Z on instance f676e776, what input it was built from and how large it was, with evidence (source trace plus the lifecycle panic record and any correlating diagnostics). Inferences are marked as such.

A fix lands that bounds or streams that output, so no single unbounded buffer is built or written, plus protection against recurrence (e.g. a size cap with a typed refusal, or chunked writes). Regression tests exercise the oversized input and show no panic and a bounded allocation.
The full gate passes on the landed tree with a clean review pair. A post-restart observation on the installed build records no recurrence of the panic under ordinary load.
